high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Opens Second Liquidity Channel, Supports Banking System Liquidity
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam announced USD/VND swap operations with credit institutions and foreign bank branches on June 1, with a 14-day tenor. The SBV bought USD spot and sold USD forward, with spot buying rate at 23,932 VND/USD and forward selling rate at 23,944 VND/USD. Maximum transaction size reached 1 billion USD, equivalent to approximately 23,932 trillion VND injected into the market if fully utilized. The 12 VND/USD spread between forward and spot rates implies an annualized cost of about 1.3%. Combined with 14-day USD interbank rates around 3.7% annually, this creates an implicit VND funding cost of approximately 5% per year through the swap channel. This represents the SBV's second major liquidity support tool, complementing open market operations, as overnight VND rates surged to 11%.

high.title: Overnight Interest Rates Surge to 11%, State Bank of Vietnam Pumps VND Aggressively
high.summary: VND interbank rates spiked across short-term tenors on June 1, with overnight rates jumping 4 percentage points to 11% annually. Two-week and one-month rates rose 0.1 and 0.15 percentage points to 7.5% and 7.75% respectively, while one-week rates held steady at 7.4%. USD rates remained stable with overnight at 3.65%, one-week at 3.7%, and one-month slightly up 0.02 points to 3.81%. In response, the SBV aggressively supported VND liquidity through open market operations on June 2, offering a total 46,000 billion VND across different tenors: 20,000 billion VND for 7 days, 12,000 billion for 35 days, and 14,000 billion for 56 days, all at 4.5% annual rate. The auction resulted in 15,218 trillion VND accepted. This aggressive liquidity injection signals the central bank's commitment to maintaining monetary stability amid tightening market conditions.

medium.title: Relaxing Credit for "Essential Real Estate Segments"
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam issued guidance to 25 commercial banks on adjusting credit growth calculations for priority real estate sectors including social housing, industrial parks, and export processing zones. From January 1 to December 31, 2026, incremental lending to these three sectors will not count toward real estate credit when determining sector growth limits. This creates additional room for banks to expand lending to support social welfare and industrial development goals.

medium.title: Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang Appointed Chairman of International Financial Center Steering Committee
medium.summary: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung chaired a meeting on continuing the development of Vietnam's International Financial Center. The center operates under a "one center, two destinations" model with National Assembly Resolution 222/2025/QH15 and eight government decrees providing the legal framework. The PM emphasized creating breakthrough mechanisms to quickly deliver key International Financial Center products.

medium.title: New Regulations from July 1: Will Terminate Operations of Bank Branches and Transaction Offices
medium.summary: New circular amendments effective July 1 grant the SBV Governor authority to force closure of domestic commercial bank branches, while regional SBV directors can terminate representative offices and business units. Grounds include false information in establishment applications leading to incorrect assessment of establishment conditions.

medium.title: Latest Savings Interest Rate Table June 3
medium.summary: LPBank reduced online deposit rates across 6-25 month terms by 0.05-0.2 percentage points. The 12-month rate dropped 0.1 points to 6.9%, no longer maintaining 7% for online 12-month deposits. The 24-25 month term saw the largest cut of 0.2 points to 7%, now LPBank's highest online rate. Despite cuts, LPBank remains in the market's leading rate group.
